Windows is a supported platform. Everything else in this release exists to
make that true.

Still an **alpha**. Nothing here is a stability promise.

## Highlights

**Cairn runs on Windows.** The CLI and daemon previously spoke over a Unix
domain socket, which is the single reason Windows was excluded. They now speak
over a named pipe when built for Windows, behind the same interface — the
protocol, the store, the capture pipeline and the Claude Code integration are
unchanged and not platform-specific. An `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` archive is
published alongside the macOS and Linux ones.

**Windows is covered by the same tests, not a smaller set.** The full suite
runs on `windows-latest` in CI: 180 of the 182 tests that run on Linux. The two
that do not are a `SIGKILL`-and-recover pair that identify processes with
`pgrep` and end them with `kill(2)`; they are skipped rather than faked,
because a Windows equivalent that is not carefully verified proves less than
nothing. Everything else — daemon lifecycle, restart recovery, concurrent
sessions, hook fail-soft, capture latency budgets, twelve clients racing a cold
store — runs there.

**`cairn update` works on Windows.** Binaries carry `.exe`, and Windows will
not let a running executable be overwritten in place, so the current binary is
renamed aside before the new one takes its path. `cairn` and `cairnd` are still
replaced together, and the archive is still checked against its published
digest before anything is installed.

## Fixed

- **`cairn` no longer leaks its standard handles into the daemon it starts.**
  Windows `CreateProcess` hands a child *every* inheritable handle, not only
  the three named in `STARTUPINFO`, so redirecting the daemon's own stdio to
  `NUL` was not enough: it also received a duplicate of whatever pipe the CLI
  had been given for stdout and stderr, and held it open for as long as it
  ran. Anything reading the other end — a shell pipeline, or the agent running
  a capture hook — waited for an EOF that could not arrive while the daemon
  lived. The inherit flag is now cleared across the spawn.
- The named-pipe client waits out `ERROR_PIPE_BUSY` instead of concluding no
  daemon is listening, so a burst of concurrent hooks queues rather than each
  trying to start a daemon of its own.

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Status |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon, `aarch64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| macOS (Intel, `x86_64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| Linux (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Linux (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Windows (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) | **Supported, new** |

## Upgrading from alpha.2

`cairn update` fetches and replaces both binaries for you. It does not restart
the daemon — it prints the two commands below, and you run them:

```bash
cairn daemon stop && cairn daemon start
```

Your local state is kept. The SQLite store migrates in place, and linked
projects, memory, tasks, sessions and handoffs survive the upgrade, as does the
Claude Code integration.

## Install

Download the archive for your platform, verify it, and put the binaries on your
PATH. `cairn` and `cairnd` must live in the same directory — `cairn` starts the
daemon itself.

macOS and Linux:

```bash
VERSION=0.1.0-alpha.3
TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin   # or x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS

tar -xzf cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairn cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairnd /usr/local/bin/
```

Windows, in PowerShell — the archive is a `.zip`:

```powershell
$VERSION = "0.1.0-alpha.3"
$TARGET = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"

Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v$VERSION/cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET.zip" -OutFile cairn.zip
Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v$VERSION/SHA256SUMS" -OutFile SHA256SUMS

Expand-Archive cairn.zip -DestinationPath .
mkdir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn" -Force
Copy-Item "cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET\cairn.exe","cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET\cairnd.exe" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn"
setx PATH "$env:PATH;$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn"
```

Open a new terminal so the PATH change takes effect. Then, inside a Git
repository, on any platform:

```bash
cairn init
cairn connect claude-code
```

## Container images

Only the server-side components ship as images. The local agent is native by
design.

```
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-server:0.1.0-alpha.3
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-web:0.1.0-alpha.3
```

Both are also published under an immutable `sha-<short-sha>` tag and built for
`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. There is deliberately no `latest` tag for a
pre-release. An example stack is in
[`deploy/docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/blob/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml).

## Verifying what you downloaded

- `SHA256SUMS` covers every archive, `.tar.gz` and `.zip` alike.
- `SBOM.spdx.json` describes the release contents.
- Archives and images carry GitHub build provenance attestations:

```bash
gh attestation verify cairn-v0.1.0-alpha.3-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip --repo Vellixia/Cairn
```

## Known limitations

- **Alpha.** Expect defects. Do not depend on this for anything you cannot
  reconstruct.
- **Pre-1.0 compatibility.** APIs, storage schemas and the wire protocol may
  change without a deprecation period.
- On Windows the stored API token is only as private as the user-profile
  directory holding it. The `0600` mode Cairn sets on Unix has no Windows
  equivalent, and no explicit ACL is applied yet.
- Server-sync tests need a PostgreSQL service container, so that suite runs on
  Linux only. The shared server and web UI are unchanged in this release.
- Sharing requires running your own Cairn server; no hosted service exists.
